title: Eval: 6 real snipe recall gaps after benchmark spec cleanup
description:
After fixing 11 benchmark spec bugs (snipe-0x5, snipe-2in, plus the May 6 batch in commits 2e90d2c/c9f2508/b1e3c06), 6 real recall gaps remain. These require snipe engineering, not YAML edits.

By failure mode:

CALLERS RECALL (cross-pkg call graph):
- orca-callers-01 — 'callers Store.Save' returns test files + cmd handlers but misses internal/kg/linker/linker.go and internal/kg/mgmt/service.go where Save is reached via saveIfModified / SaveNugget. May be missing transitive-to-direct links or pkg-boundary edges.

SEARCH RECALL (text + semantic):
- cobra-cross-01 — search 'Args' / 'PositionalArgs' doesn't surface ExactArgs (top-level func, common term).
- fzf-cross-01 — search 'matcher' doesn't surface FuzzyMatchV2 (the actual matcher impl).
- orca-search-04 — search 'staleness' returns text hits with name='staleness' rather than enclosing symbols (Checker.GetCurationHints, Checker.findStaleNuggets). Structural mismatch: search results don't carry enclosing-func metadata.
- orca-search-08 — search 'GoSymbolService' returns no snipe results (rg fallback only). Index miss on the type itself.

REFS LIMIT/ORDER:
- cobra-refs-01 — 'refs Command' returns 50 results but command.go (the def file) isn't among the unique files in the eval's found_files. Manual run had command.go in the basenames; eval doesn't. Likely --limit ordering issue or refs default sort biasing away from def file.

Score now: 66/72 scored pass = 92% (was 57/72 = 79%). These six are the floor.

Suggested investigation order:
1. orca-search-04 (structural — search results need enclosing-symbol field)
2. orca-search-08 + orca-callers-01 (index/recall)
3. cobra-cross-01, fzf-cross-01 (search relevance)
4. cobra-refs-01 (refs ordering/limit)
notes: orca-search-04 partially fixed (May 6): added FindEnclosingSymbol with doc-comment fallback. GetCurationHints now resolves. findStaleNuggets still missing — 'staleness' doesn't appear near it lexically. Needs vague-concept semantic fallback. Score: 92%→95.9%. 3 failures left: orca-callers-01, cobra-cross-01, fzf-cross-01.

title: Distance from main sequence: D = |A + I - 1|

Depends on A and I being available.

title: Architecture review metrics suite
description:
Add architecture-review metrics to snipe beyond the existing PageRank/boundary/diagram set. Goal: support 'is this codebase architecturally healthy' assessment with quantitative signals — coupling, instability, cohesion, abstractness — at the package level.

Triggered by trixi arch-review work where snipe metrics had useful signal (PageRank for hot paths, boundary for split planning) but lacked Martin-style coupling/stability metrics that drive most arch-health frameworks. Reviewers fell back to ad-hoc grep + manual counting.

## Scope

Per-package metrics, computed from the existing dependency graph:

- **Ca (afferent coupling)** — count of packages that import this package. High Ca = many depend on it; changes ripple.
- **Ce (efferent coupling)** — count of packages this package imports. High Ce = depends on much; brittle to others' changes.
- **I (instability)** — Ce / (Ca + Ce). 0 = max stable (only depended-on), 1 = max unstable (only depends-on). Both extremes are valid; middle is the warning zone.
- **A (abstractness)** — abstract types (interfaces) / total types in package. Pairs with I.
- **D (distance from main sequence)** — |A + I - 1|. Martin's 'painful' (D≈0 is concrete-stable utility, D≈1 is abstract-unstable junk-drawer). Single scalar that flags both.
- **LCOM4 (lack of cohesion)** — connected components of the symbol graph within a package, where edges are 'calls or shares a field.' >1 = package wants to split.
- **Cyclomatic complexity rollups** — already computed per-function by gocyclo; sum/p95/max per package gives a 'hot package' signal independent of the dependency graph.

## Output shape

- New 'snipe metrics' subcommand or column extension. Default JSON; pretty table for TTY.
- Wire into existing 'snipe context' so arch-review prompts get these for free.
- Thresholds documented (D > 0.7 = flag, LCOM4 > 1 = split candidate, I=0 + Ca=0 = orphan).

## Non-goals

- Cross-encoder/ML quality scoring.
- Authoring 'arch fitness functions' DSL — just expose the numbers.
- Java/JVM-specific metrics that don't translate to Go.

Acceptance: a single 'snipe metrics --pkg=X' run returns Ca, Ce, I, A, D, LCOM4, and cyclo-rollup for X; arch-review prompts can cite these instead of hand-counting.
close_reason: cyclo rollups shipped; arch-review metrics suite complete (pagerank, hits, coupling, instability, abstractness, distance, lcom4, cyclo)

title: Incremental reindex misses package_docs changes (status=fresh lies)
description:
Editing a Go file's package doc comment does not refresh the package_docs row on subsequent index runs, even though 'snipe status' reports state=fresh.

Repro (trixi repo):
- app/cmd/trixi/doc.go rewritten 2026-04-16 (commit c1ce351b) — first sentence changed from 'a single binary for managing a personal knowledge graph' to 'a single binary for an AI workmate and coach that knows you and gets better over time. The knowledge graph is infrastructure; the relationship is the product.'
- snipe ran reindex 2026-04-27 (meta.indexed_at). 'snipe status' returns state=fresh.
- sqlite3 .snipe/index.db 'SELECT indexed_at FROM package_docs WHERE pkg_path="github.com/dkoosis/trixi/cmd/trixi"' returns 2026-03-20 — stale by 5+ weeks.
- 'snipe context' surfaces the stale tagline as the project description.

Expected: package_docs.indexed_at and doc text update whenever the underlying file's package comment changes. Either fingerprinting must include comment changes, or incremental reindex must always re-scan package_docs for touched files.

Caught by dk during a doc.go audit conversation. The wrong tagline propagated into 'snipe context' output, which then misleads agents orienting on the project.

Acceptance:
- Editing a package doc comment and running 'snipe index' (no --force) updates package_docs.indexed_at and doc within one pass.
- 'snipe status' freshness is honest: state=fresh implies all derived tables are current with the file fingerprints.
- Add a regression test that mutates a package comment, reindexes, and asserts package_docs reflects the new text.

Verified on trixi — orphan github.com/dkoosis/trixi/cmd/trixi row removed, snipe context now shows the fresh app/cmd/trixi tagline. title: M3: cross-reference deps x refs for module-split planning
description: Answer: 'if package X lives in module A and Y in module B, which symbols cross the boundary?' Neither `deps` (package-level) nor `refs` (symbol-level) answers directly. New query combining package sets with symbol-level cross-boundary refs. Hard: query surface design, output shape, perf on large graphs.
design:
## Question answered
'If I split packages {A} into one module and {B} into another, which symbols cross the boundary, in which direction, and from where?'

## Data shape (already in index)
- symbols.pkg_path → owning package
- refs.symbol_id → referenced (target) symbol
- refs.enclosing_id → enclosing (source) symbol
- 3-way join: refs ⨝ symbols(target) ⨝ symbols(enclosing) gives (src_pkg, tgt_pkg, symbol, kind, file:line)

## Command surface
`snipe boundary <set-a> <set-b>` — name signals intent better than 'xrefs' or extending deps.
- Sets: glob patterns, repeatable. `snipe boundary 'internal/store/...' 'internal/query'`
- Default output: bidirectional summary (A→B counts and B→A counts, grouped by symbol kind)
- `--direction=a-to-b|b-to-a|both` (default both)
- `--detailed` → per-symbol with ref locations
- `--exclude-tests` (default true; module-split planning rarely cares about test refs)
- `--format=json` for orca consumption

## Output (default, Claude-optimized)
Compact text: 'A→B: 12 refs to 4 symbols (3 funcs, 1 type)' then top symbols by ref count.
`--detailed` adds per-ref file:line.

## Perf
Single SQL with two joins. snipe's own graph: ~5k symbols, ~30k refs. Indexed on pkg_path. Target <500ms.

## Open questions
1. Glob syntax: doublestar (`internal/store/...`) or prefix-match? Lean doublestar — matches deps.go conventions.
2. Self-refs within a set: include or filter? Filter by default (boundary = ACROSS sets).
3. Transitive vs direct: direct only for v1. Transitive is a follow-up.

## Out of scope (v1)
- Suggesting split lines automatically
- Counting bytes/complexity of the boundary
- Visualizing (that's diagram bead snipe-fc9 territory)

title: Adopt graph metrics from beads_viewer (PageRank, betweenness, HITS, SCC) for code graphs
description:
Reference: github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer (pkg/graph) implements 9 graph metrics for issue dependency graphs. The same algorithms apply directly to snipe's import and call graphs, where they answer architect questions:

- PageRank on import graph → foundational packages (recursive importance)
- Betweenness centrality → bottleneck packages/funcs (everything routes through them)
- HITS hubs/authorities → entry points vs. core types (formalizes what `context` does heuristically today)
- Tarjan SCC → import cycles, mutual recursion clusters
- Topological sort → safe init order, refactor ordering
- Eigenvector / degree centrality → influence scoring

Primary value is as INPUT TO CURATION for the diagram renderer (sibling bead snipe-fc9): 'show top 20 nodes by PageRank, hide the rest' is what makes large-graph diagrams readable. Secondary value: `snipe metrics` standalone command for architects.

What does NOT transfer: their critical-path is duration-weighted (issues have effort estimates); code edges are unweighted unless we invent weights (LOC? churn? complexity?). Skip critical-path until weighting story exists.
design:
Implementation options:
1. Vendor pkg/graph from beads_viewer (MIT license — check)
2. Reimplement against snipe's existing graph schema
3. Use gonum/graph for the algorithms

Lean toward option 2 or 3. beads_viewer's graph type is shaped around issue nodes; snipe's graphs are package/symbol-shaped. Adapter cost likely exceeds reimplementation cost for a small set of well-known algorithms.

Storage: precompute on `snipe index`, persist in SQLite. Recompute only on full reindex. Centrality scores are small (one float per node).
acceptance_criteria:
- `snipe metrics --kind=pagerank` ranks packages by import-graph PageRank
- `snipe metrics --kind=betweenness` identifies bottleneck symbols
- `snipe metrics --kind=cycles` reports import cycles via Tarjan SCC
- Metrics are available as a curation input to `snipe diagram` (--top-n by-pagerank)
- Computed at index time, persisted, queried in <50ms
close_reason: All 9 children shipped: graph metrics (PageRank/Brandes/HITS/SCC/degree/eigenvector/topo) + snipe metrics command + diagram renderer consumer with --top-n by PageRank trim.

title: Diagram renderer: D2 export from snipe graphs
description:
Snipe already has the underlying graphs (imports, calls, refs, lifecycle, context roles) but only emits text/JSON. Add a D2 renderer layer for visual consumption.

Scope is the renderer + curation, not new graph data. The hard part is curation: raw call graphs are hairballs. Use existing role annotations (entry_point, api_boundary, persistence) from `snipe context` to render the architectural backbone, not every edge.

Three opinionated subcommands rather than one generic dumper:
- `snipe diagram arch` — package layering with role annotations
- `snipe diagram flow <entry>` — depth-limited call graph from one entry point
- `snipe diagram lifecycle <Type>` — render existing CRUD lifecycle data visually

D2 only. No Mermaid, no DOT. Single output format keeps the surface small.

Default = Claude-readable summary + the D2 source. `--format svg` shells out to d2 CLI if installed.
design:
D1: Claude is primary consumer. Diagrams are a side-channel for humans, not the default. Bare `snipe diagram` should still print useful text, with diagram source as a follow-up section.

D4: token budget. Diagram source can be large — gate behind explicit subcommand, never auto-include in other outputs.

Curation > completeness. Limit nodes by depth, by role, or by PageRank-style centrality (see sibling bead). A 30-node diagram is useful; a 300-node diagram is not.
acceptance_criteria:
- `snipe diagram arch` outputs valid D2 for snipe's own repo, renders cleanly via d2 CLI
- `snipe diagram flow main` produces a depth-3 D2 call graph
- `snipe diagram lifecycle <Type>` renders existing lifecycle CRUD data as D2
- Default output remains Claude-optimized text; D2 source is additive
- `--format svg` shells out to d2 if installed, errors cleanly if not
close_reason: Closed

After perf-tag sweep (snipe-5hu), assess whether to enable style/opinionated/experimental too. These are chatty (~115 issues across the three) and may produce false-positive churn — evaluate value vs noise before enabling.

title: trace: dedicated string-literal / env-var tracking command
description: snipe trace 'TRIXI_VOYAGE_API_KEY' — combine ripgrep with context about each occurrence (function calls, assignments, comparisons). Currently search finds them but no surrounding semantics. Closes #126 M1.

title: feat(edit): --dry-run unified-diff preview output
description: M6 from #126. snipe edit defaults to preview but the format isn't documented and isn't a unified diff. Emit a real diff on --dry-run so Claude can review before applying.
close_reason: Already implemented — edit defaults to preview (--apply to commit); results[0].diff carries unified diff. help text: 'shows a preview without modifying files. The response includes a unified diff'.

title: feat(pack): snipe pack <package> — package-level pack output
description: M4 from #126. Like 'pack <symbol>' but for packages: exports, imports, dep count, test count, LOC, key types. Overlaps with 'pkg'; needs design call on whether to extend pkg or add a new verb.
close_reason: Already implemented — 'snipe pack internal/query' produces package-level pack: dir, files, loc, tests, exports, imports, dependents, key_types. cmd/pack.go handles package-path args.

title: feat(trace): snipe trace <string> for env-var/config-key tracking
description: M1 from #126. Composite cmd that wraps ripgrep search with context: where the literal appears, in what calls/assignments. Useful for tracing TRIXI_VOYAGE_API_KEY-style strings that def/refs can't see.
close_reason: trace command shipped: literal refs + enclosing + callers, substring fallback, lits routing fix

title: research(embed): improve vague-intent semantic search
description: Eval shows 80.8% symbol accuracy; gap is in vague-intent queries that matter most for orientation. Plan: enrich embedding input (doc+sig+pkg-narrative+caller-context), consider re-ranking, measure with eval harness. Blocked on telemetry for ground truth. Research+plan first; no implementation until eval signal exists.

title: Issue #112: Improve semantic search for vague-intent queries
description: Embedding pipeline improvements (richer input: doc+sig+pkg narrative+caller context, possible re-rank). Blocked on telemetry for ground-truth validation. Defer until telemetry exists. Depends on #105 (package narratives).

value: When closing an epic, close its open children in the same pass — don't leave orphans. Check deps for siblings the epic's work may have resolved.
backwards compatibility is NOT relevant on snipe — no migration shims, no forward-only constraints, break schema freely

Epic/singleton from a GH issue → set gh_issue=<N> metadata at create (number only, no #). Children inherit via parent; don't duplicate. Lookup: bd query -a --json | jq '.[]|select(.metadata.gh_issue=="N")'. On close: include 'Closes #N' in commit or gh issue close N.

Claude Agent tool with isolation: worktree does NOT reliably create isolated branches — observed multiple parallel agents on snipe collapsing to same /Users/vcto/projects/snipe (lowercase) workdir on main. Agents serialized via git pull --rebase + push retries. Strategy: (a) for schema-touching parallel work, sequence don't parallelize; (b) for additive work, accept rebase races and instruct agents to retry; (c) put new code in separate files where possible to minimize text conflicts.
